RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

The panel's composition alone proves little — in many hospital hierarchies four male senior managers is simply what the org chart produces. It's context, not evidence.

What's more notable is the pattern: your formal qualifications appear stronger, and the stated justification leans on a vague phrase ("broad leadership experience") that is hard to verify and easy to apply selectively. That, plus two weeks of silence on a reasonable request, is what deserves attention.

So pursue the written reasons — in writing, with a deadline, citing any applicable policy or statutory right. Ask what criteria were weighted and how each candidate scored. Mention the panel composition only as background if the reasons turn out to be unsatisfactory. Lead with it and you'll look like you're guessing.
